E09.name: Dumbbell Forearm Pronation

muscleEvidence.note: Pronator teres (PT) and pronator quadratus (PQ) are the pronators (OpenStax table: PT prime mover 'turns hand palm-down', PQ 'assists'). EMG evidence on which dominates is mixed and load-dependent: Kondi 2026 (n=4, isometric, neutral forearm) saw PQ more active than PT at the lowest torque and PT rising proportionally more as torque increased; Gordon 2004 (cited secondhand in Ibanez-Gimeno 2014) reported PT as the primary agonist in maximal resisted pronation. Takamori 2024 (MRI, elbow extended) identified PT as pronation agonist with ECU and extensor digitorum as load-dependent synergists. Fukunaga 2023 (band pronation, forearm on thigh) recorded PT 73.0 %MVC and FDS 63.9 %MVC vs FCU 27.4 %MVC. All of these muscles fall under the 'forearms' key.

E09.appliedChanges: None: no opened source supported a change.

studyAssociation.summary: No study of seated dumbbell-lever pronation was found. Closest: elastic-band pronation with the forearm on the thigh (Fukunaga 2023, EMG of FCU/FDS/PT only, 10 men), isometric loaded-rod pronation (Kondi 2026, n=4, includes PQ), and isotonic weight-and-string pronation with the elbow extended (Takamori 2024, MRI). None is longitudinal; none measured hypertrophy or load norms.

resistanceProfile.note: Sourced: the external rotational torque is the load multiplied by its distance from the forearm rotation axis (Kondi 2026 produced 0.98-3.43 Nm by hanging 1 kg at 10-35 cm), so grip position along the dumbbell changes the load. PT rotational efficiency (model) is maximal near forearm neutral and minimal at the extremes of pronation-supination (Ibanez-Gimeno 2014). The angle-by-angle torque curve of a dumbbell held at one end: not established by sources found.

E10.name: Dumbbell Forearm Supination

muscleEvidence.note: Supinator is a supination agonist: OpenStax lists supinator as prime mover ('turns hand palm-up'); Takamori 2024 (MRI, elbow extended) found supinator active even at 5 %MVC; Kondi 2026 (n=4) found supinator more active than biceps at the lowest torque. Brachioradialis is described (Takamori, citing literature) as rotating the forearm toward neutral - also under 'forearms'.

At the spec's ~90 deg elbow angle the sources treat biceps as a principal supinator, not merely a helper: OpenStax lists biceps brachii as prime mover with 'flexion; supination'; Gulecyuz 2017 states supination is produced by supinator and biceps 'where the biceps brachii muscle mainly contributes to the strength', calls 90 deg elbow flexion the position of maximal biceps impact, and measured greater isometric supination strength at 90 deg than with the elbow extended (105 adults); Kondi 2026 saw biceps activity rise proportionally more than supinator as torque increased. Takamori 2024 (citing literature) notes biceps supination torque is reduced to almost zero with the elbow extended.

E10.appliedChanges: Promoted biceps to primary: opened sources describe it as a main supination torque producer with the elbow at 90 degrees, its share rising with load.

studyAssociation.summary: No study of dumbbell-lever supination found. Related: isometric loaded-rod supination EMG (Kondi 2026, n=4, elbow angle not stated), isotonic weight-and-string supination with elbow extended (Takamori 2024, MRI; biceps not measured), isometric dynamometer supination strength by elbow angle (Gulecyuz 2017). O'Sullivan & Gallwey 2002 (elbow/forearm angle EMG) and Naito 1995 could not be opened.

resistanceProfile.note: Sourced: rotational torque = load x distance from the forearm axis (Kondi 2026 setup), so hand position along the dumbbell changes the load; isometric supination strength is greater at 90 deg elbow flexion than at full extension (Gulecyuz 2017). Angle-by-angle torque curve of the one-end-held dumbbell: not established by sources found.
